decision: D-206. Every answer restates what the part's own panels teach, with the same sources.

what-is-an-erp: ERP stands for enterprise resource planning. In plain words: one system where every team works on the same records. An order is entered once, and sales, stock and accounts all read that same record.
Why do small businesses move from spreadsheets to an ERP?

Separate sheets for orders, stock and invoices stop agreeing. In the comic, a salesperson promises coffee the roastery already sold, because nobody told the stock sheet. With an ERP, everyone sees that sale at the same moment.
What is the difference between Frappe and ERPNext?
Frappe is the company. ERPNext is the ERP it makes. Think of The Coffee Company and its Ethiopian roast: one is the maker, the other is what it makes.
Selling, buying, stock and accounts, plus payroll and projects when a company is ready for them.
Is an ERP easy to set up?
No. An ERP changes how every team works, and Frappe itself says any ERP is complex to set up alone. Part 4 explains who helps with that.
who-is-behind-this: Rushabh Mehta. His family's furniture factory was struggling with a bad ERP built by a local company, so he started writing his own. His co-founders are Nabin Hait, Mohammad Umair Sayed and Prakash Hodage.
Why does it matter who makes your ERP?

You can delete a phone app. An ERP holds your orders, stock and accounts for years, and when it stops fitting how you work, someone has to change it. So check who builds it and how, like visiting a farm before a long contract.

Frappe calls itself a collective: a company its people run together. There are no reporting managers. People choose their own work and set their own pay, and decisions are made together, democratically, under a written constitution.
Where can I read how Frappe works?
Frappe publishes its culture and its story on frappe.io. The sources under this comic link to each page it draws on.
why-it-is-open-source: Yes. ERPNext's code is under an open licence and has been online since 2009. Anyone can read it, run it and change it.

Code is the written instructions software follows. Most makers keep it secret, which is called closed source. Open source software publishes its code under a licence: the written rules on what anyone may do with it.
Does open source ERPNext hold features back?
No. All of ERPNext is open. No feature is held back.
Why should a finance team care about open code?
Every screen and every total in ERPNext comes from its code. You never have to read it yourself: open means someone you trust can check it for you.
what-if-we-want-to-leave: Can you get locked in to ERPNext?
Leaving any ERP is work, but nobody can lock you in. Lock-in means only the maker can run or change your system. ERPNext's code is open, so another team can pick up the same system.
Setting the ERP up around how a company works: its warehouses, its price lists, who approves a purchase. Every one of those is a decision made with the company.
A company trained and certified to set up and support Frappe's software. If you don't get on with your partner, you can change partners, because the code is open.
On hosting: a computer that is always on and looked after, so every team reaches the same system. Frappe Cloud is the official hosting for Frappe apps. It handles setup, upgrades and monitoring.
How does Frappe make money if the code is open?
Frappe and its partners are paid for setup, hosting and support. Open code doesn't set itself up or run itself.
everything-frappe-makes: A family of apps, each for one job. ERPNext is one. Others include Frappe CRM for customers, Frappe Helpdesk for support and Frappe HR for people and payroll.
A toolkit for building business apps quickly. ERPNext was the first app built with it. Frappe built the Framework so it could build ERPNext.
What is a Frappe Cloud site?
Your company's own copy of the software, at its own web address. One site can hold several Frappe apps.
Should a company install every Frappe app on day one?
No. Having many apps doesn't mean each one fits you. Check each against how your company works.
